# pve_ceph_osd (Data Source)

Reads the metadata of one Ceph OSD from `GET /nodes/{node}/ceph/osd/{osdid}/metadata`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

data "pve_ceph_osd" "osd0" {
  node   = "pve1"
  osd_id = 0
}

output "osd0_objectstore" {
  value = data.pve_ceph_osd.osd0.osd_objectstore
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node` (String) Name of the PVE node hosting the OSD.
- `osd_id` (Number) OSD id (the numeric part of `osd.<id>`).

### Read-Only

- `back_addr` (String) Address and port used to talk to other OSDs.
- `devices` (Attributes List) Devices backing the OSD (block, db, and wal devices). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--devices))
- `encrypted` (Boolean) Whether the OSD is encrypted with LUKS via dm-crypt.
- `front_addr` (String) Address and port used to talk to clients and monitors.
- `hb_back_addr` (String) Heartbeat address and port for clients and monitors.
- `hb_front_addr` (String) Heartbeat address and port for other OSDs.
- `hostname` (String) Name of the host containing the OSD.
- `id` (String) Identifier in the form `<node>:osd.<id>`.
- `mem_usage` (Number) Proportional set size (PSS) memory usage of the OSD daemon process in bytes; 0 when the process is not running.
- `osd_data` (String) Path to the OSD's data directory.
- `osd_objectstore` (String) The object store type used by the OSD (typically `bluestore`).
- `pid` (Number) OSD process id; null when the systemd unit for this OSD is not currently running.
- `version` (String) Ceph version of the OSD service.

<a id="nestedatt--devices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `devices`

Read-Only:

- `dev_node` (String) Device node name.
- `device` (String) Kind of OSD device: `block`, `db`, or `wal`.
- `physical_device` (String) Underlying physical device(s) used by this OSD device.
- `size` (Number) Size of the OSD device in bytes.
- `support_discard` (Boolean) Whether the underlying physical device supports discard/TRIM.
- `type` (String) Type of device, for example `hdd` or `ssd`.
